title: Daily life, drinking and the secret of long life
summary: Laine says he sleeps and drinks, credits good living and the Lord for his age, and recalls a drunken night after playing for Dwyer.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Drinking what? What do you drink? I drink whiskey, milk, beer, wine, anything comes along, it's all right.
What do you attribute your old age to, Papa? How come you live to be as old as you are? How come you lasted this long? What's your secret?

Well, now that's a coincidence and a funny thing to answer, funny question to answer. I've been a good boy and a strong boy all my days. I remember being in a kind of serious trouble, nothing of that sort, and I always believed in our Lord. And I brought myself upright. Still, I smoked plenty. I drank plenty. Now, whether it's the whiskey preserved me, I don't know. I couldn't say. It might have been the Lord.
It might have been the Lord.
I played one night up in Protection Levee for Dwyer.

For Dwyer? For Dwyer up in Protection Levee. And I tell you, they had a car in my home. Is that right? Had a car in my home. And when I got home, I was almost, almost passed out the pitcher entirely. Drinking whiskey? Drinking whiskey? Drinking whiskey. I must have drank a fifth. Oh, that's a lot. I must have drank a whole fifth. Amy and Quigley and that bunch had to carry me. All them kids had to carry me. Really, carry me through the bus and leads the streetcar and from the streetcar home.
